message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $157 and a red monopoly with one house each on Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois. p2 owns the full pink monopoly for $963. p3 has no monopoly and $1187.

p4 owns two railroads and the light blue properties. I have no cash to buy unowned properties. I will end my turn.

Unmortgaging either mortgaged property would leave me with too little cash. Building another house would leave only $7, which is too risky.

Unmortgaging would not complete a set. I considered trading Vermont to p4, but they previously rejected that offer and refused to pay cash for it.

I will not chase p4 on another trade offer. I am now considering a deal with p2.

A deal with p2 offers no synergy. They already own the full pink monopoly and do not need my red properties.

Trading New York to p3 would help them complete an orange set. That is too dangerous.

I am now looking for a cash offer from another player.

I cannot buy unowned properties during a post-turn action. I am now calculating the rent values for my red properties to assess their income potential.

The rent from one house on each red property is only $90 to $100. That is too small to threaten opponents with $1000 cash. Building a second house would leave only $7, which is fatal if a card hits. I will end my turn.

I will not propose a trade. p2 sold me Illinois recently and may be wary of another deal. p4 is already organizing a boycott against funding me.

I briefly considered trading mortgaged Vermont to p4 for Connecticut. That would leave me with only two light blue properties, and Oriental is unowned so I cannot complete the set without p4's help.
